content_security_policy_enforced.title: Content-Security-Policy Enforced
content_security_policy_enforced.description: Whether the server delivers a Content-Security-Policy response header that restricts script sources (interpreted from the real content_security_policy config key). Secure=true (a restrictive CSP is present); the exposure fires when false (header absent), leaving reflected/stored/DOM XSS unmitigated at the second layer.

csp_allows_unsafe_inline_or_eval.title: CSP Allows unsafe-inline / unsafe-eval
csp_allows_unsafe_inline_or_eval.description: Interpreted-boolean reading of the composite content_security_policy directive: whether script-src permits 'unsafe-inline' or 'unsafe-eval' (or a wildcard default-src *). Modeled as an interpreted boolean rather than a substring/regex match because the secure CSP string can legitimately mention these tokens while excluding them. Secure=false (CSP forbids unsafe inline/eval, using nonces/hashes); the exposure fires when true, which neutralizes CSP as an XSS control.

trusted_types_enforced.title: Trusted Types Enforced
trusted_types_enforced.description: Whether the CSP enforces Trusted Types via require-trusted-types-for 'script' (interpreted from the csp_trusted_types config key), forcing dangerous DOM sinks (innerHTML, eval) through a sanitizing policy. Secure=true; the exposure fires when false, leaving DOM-based XSS sinks unguarded.

contextual_output_encoding_applied.title: Contextual Output Encoding Applied
contextual_output_encoding_applied.description: Interpreted-boolean reading of the output_encoding_xss config/review item: whether all untrusted data is rendered via context-aware output encoding / auto-escaping templating (no raw innerHTML/document.write/dangerouslySetInnerHTML/v-html of user data, DOMPurify on any HTML). This is the foundational first-layer XSS defense. Secure=true; the exposure fires when false (user data reaches a sink unsanitized).

x_content_type_options_nosniff_set.title: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff Set
x_content_type_options_nosniff_set.description: Whether the server sends X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff (interpreted from the x_content_type_options config key), stopping MIME-sniffing of responses into executable types — a class of XSS where user-controlled content is reinterpreted as script. Secure=true; the exposure fires when false (header absent).

stored_in_js_accessible_storage.title: Tokens / PII Stored in JS-Accessible Storage
stored_in_js_accessible_storage.description: Interpreted: a session token, JWT, refresh token, or PII is persisted in localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB or any other JavaScript-readable client storage (true = INSECURE). When true, injected script or a hostile extension can read and replay the token or harvest PII, and the data survives the session on a shared/compromised device. Secure value is false (tokens held only in HttpOnly cookies or a BFF pattern; no PII in JS-readable storage). Consolidates the rule-1 token-storage trigger and the rule-6 PII-persistence trigger.

cookie_httponly_flag.title: Session Cookie HttpOnly Flag
cookie_httponly_flag.description: Whether the session/auth cookie carries the HttpOnly attribute (true = SECURE; fires on is_false). When false, document.cookie / injected script can exfiltrate the session token.

cookie_secure_flag.title: Session Cookie Secure Flag
cookie_secure_flag.description: Whether the session cookie carries the Secure attribute so it is only transmitted over HTTPS (true = SECURE; fires on is_false). When false, the cookie can leak to a network attacker over cleartext and be replayed, enabling session hijacking. Consolidates the duplicate session_cookie_secure_flag from the token-theft and insecure-transport vectors.

samesite_mode.title: Session Cookie SameSite Mode
samesite_mode.description: The SameSite attribute value on the session cookie. Positive condition on the insecure value: eq 'None' fires (cookie sent on cross-site requests, widening replay/CSRF surface); 'Strict' and 'Lax' are the non-firing secure values.

access_token_short_lived_rotated.title: Access Tokens Short-Lived and Rotated
access_token_short_lived_rotated.description: Interpreted: access tokens delivered to the client are short-lived (minutes) with refresh-token rotation and server-side revocation (true = SECURE; fires on is_false). When false, a stolen token remains valid long enough to fully hijack the account and cannot be revoked.

hsts_enabled.title: HSTS Enabled
hsts_enabled.description: Whether the application sends a Strict-Transport-Security response header with a long max-age (e.g. >= 63072000) and includeSubDomains, forcing the browser onto HTTPS. Secure value is true; when false the browser can be SSL-stripped/downgraded and session cookies/tokens travel in cleartext to a network adversary (a missing header or max-age=0 is interpreted as false).

upgrade_insecure_requests_enabled.title: Upgrade-Insecure-Requests Enabled
upgrade_insecure_requests_enabled.description: Whether the Content-Security-Policy includes the upgrade-insecure-requests directive, instructing the browser to rewrite http:// subresource requests to https://. Secure value is true; when false the page relies solely on no-mixed-content discipline and is exposed to mixed content that downgrades parts of the page to cleartext.

mixed_content_present.title: Active Mixed Content Present
mixed_content_present.description: Whether the page actually references http:// scripts, iframes, or other active subresources (active mixed content). INSECURE-when-true attestation: secure value is false (no mixed content). When true, an attacker can read/modify the downgraded cleartext portion and ride the session even if HSTS is present.

subresource_integrity_enforced.title: Subresource Integrity Enforced
subresource_integrity_enforced.description: Whether every cross-origin/CDN <script> and <link> tag carries a Subresource Integrity (integrity='sha384-...') attribute plus crossorigin, so the browser rejects a tampered/swapped third-party resource. Secure (true) when all external resources are SRI-pinned; the exposure fires (is_false) when a CDN script has no integrity attribute — the Magecart-style supply-chain-exposed state.

dependency_versions_pinned_lockfile.title: Dependency Versions Pinned via Lockfile
dependency_versions_pinned_lockfile.description: Whether the client-side JS dependency tree is pinned via a committed lockfile (package-lock.json / pnpm-lock.yaml / yarn.lock) with exact resolved versions and integrity hashes, so a compromised upstream npm package cannot be silently swapped into the build. Secure (true) when the lockfile is pinned and authoritative; the exposure fires (is_false) when dependencies are unpinned/floating.

dependency_vulnerability_scanning_enable.title: Dependency Vulnerability Scanning Enabled
dependency_vulnerability_scanning_enable.description: Whether automated Software Composition Analysis / dependency scanning (e.g. npm audit, Dependabot, SCA tooling) runs against the client-side dependency tree to surface known-vulnerable or malicious packages before release. Secure (true) when SCA gating is enabled with no unresolved high/critical advisories; the exposure fires (is_false) when the dependency tree is unaudited.

frame_ancestors_restricted.title: CSP frame-ancestors Restricted
frame_ancestors_restricted.description: Interpreted from the Content-Security-Policy response header: true when frame-ancestors is set to 'none' or 'self' (the modern primary anti-clickjacking control), false when the CSP frame-ancestors directive is absent or permissive — leaving the page embeddable in an attacker-controlled iframe for UI-redress. Secure value is true; fires on false.

x_frame_options_set.title: X-Frame-Options Set
x_frame_options_set.description: Interpreted from the X-Frame-Options response header: true when set to DENY or SAMEORIGIN (the legacy anti-framing fallback for older clients), false when the header is absent. With frame-ancestors also missing, the page is framable by any origin. Secure value is true; fires on false.

cors_allow_origin_wildcard.title: CORS Allow-Origin Wildcard
cors_allow_origin_wildcard.description: Interpreted from the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header: true when the header is set to '*' (wildcard) rather than an explicit allow-listed origin. A wildcard ACAO lets any origin issue cross-origin reads; combined with credentials it exposes authenticated responses. Insecure when true; the hardened config echoes a single validated trusted origin (false).

cors_origin_reflected.title: CORS Origin Reflected Unvalidated
cors_origin_reflected.description: Interpreted from CORS behavior: true when the server reflects an arbitrary request Origin back into Access-Control-Allow-Origin without validating it against an allow-list (e.g. a spoofed 'https://evil.example' Origin is echoed). Reflected-origin CORS is functionally equivalent to a credentialed wildcard. Insecure when true; secure servers only emit a validated allow-listed origin (false).

cors_allow_credentials.title: CORS Allow-Credentials Enabled
cors_allow_credentials.description: Interpreted from the Access-Control-Allow-Credentials response header: true when credentialed cross-origin requests are permitted (cookies/Authorization forwarded). Only safe when paired with an explicit, validated origin allow-list; a secondary trigger that, combined with the absence of an allow-list, exposes authenticated responses to a malicious origin.

cors_origin_allowlist_strict.title: CORS Origin Allowlist Strict
cors_origin_allowlist_strict.description: Interpreted from CORS configuration: true when Access-Control-Allow-Origin is emitted only after validating the request Origin against an explicit, finite allow-list (with Vary: Origin). This is the secure state — credentialed CORS without it is the exposure, so the rule fires on its absence (is_false) only when credentials are also allowed.

postmessage_origin_validated.title: postMessage Origin Validated
postmessage_origin_validated.description: Interpreted from client-code review of window.postMessage receivers: true when every addEventListener('message', ...) handler checks event.origin against a trusted allow-list before acting on the message. Secure state is true; a handler with no event.origin check lets a malicious frame/window inject or steal cross-frame data, so the rule fires on its absence (is_false).

postmessage_target_origin_wildcard.title: postMessage Target-Origin Wildcard
postmessage_target_origin_wildcard.description: Interpreted from client-code review of window.postMessage senders: true when any postMessage call uses a '*' targetOrigin instead of an explicit https origin, broadcasting the message (potentially sensitive data) to whatever origin currently occupies the target frame. Insecure when true; the hardened code pins an explicit targetOrigin (false).

cache_control_no_store_on_sensitive.title: Cache-Control no-store on Sensitive Responses
cache_control_no_store_on_sensitive.description: Whether authenticated/sensitive responses (PII or token-bearing) carry Cache-Control: no-store (with max-age=0), preventing the sensitive payload from lingering in the browser disk cache, back-button history, or shared proxies. Secure value is 'no-store, max-age=0' on sensitive responses (true); insecure is a cacheable sensitive response with no/public/long-max-age Cache-Control (false).

sensitive_field_autocomplete_off.title: Sensitive Field Autocomplete Disabled
sensitive_field_autocomplete_off.description: Whether secret/sensitive input fields (passwords, MFA codes, account/card numbers) disable browser autofill/credential persistence via autocomplete=off (or autocomplete="new-password" where appropriate), preventing the browser from caching the secret on a shared device. Secure value is true (autocomplete disabled on secret fields → non-firing); insecure is false (secrets retained by the browser's autofill store).

server_side_input_validation_enforced.title: Server-Side Input Validation Enforced
server_side_input_validation_enforced.description: Whether the server independently re-validates all client-supplied input (types, ranges, business-rule constraints) on every state-changing/sensitive endpoint, rather than relying on client-side/UI validation. Secure value is true (re-validated server-side); the exposure fires when false, because an attacker can modify the client or call the API directly to bypass any client-only validation.

authz_enforced_server_side_centrally.title: Authorization Enforced Server-Side Centrally
authz_enforced_server_side_centrally.description: Whether the server enforces authentication and authorization for every sensitive action server-side, independent of the untrusted client (no reliance on UI hiding of privileged controls). Secure value is true; the exposure fires when false, because an attacker can drive a non-browser client or replay a privileged call to access functionality the UI merely hid.

client_asserted_state_trusted_serverside.title: Client-Asserted State Trusted Server-Side
client_asserted_state_trusted_serverside.description: Interpreted boolean: whether the server honors roles, privilege flags, or authorization decisions asserted by the client (e.g. an isAdmin field in the request body, a client-supplied role header, or a JWT claim the client can edit) instead of deriving them from a server-side trusted session/store. This is the INSECURE state, so true is the firing condition; the secure posture is false (server derives all authorization from trusted server-side state).
